name: jazz-phrasing
style: 1997 East Coast hardcore hip hop, solo male rapper who phrases like a bebop horn soloist: lays back behind the snare, stretches a syllable then rushes the next three, accents land like a jazz drummer's snare hits, smooth internal multisyllabic rhymes, calm conversational menace, a held breath before every punchline. Voice: heavyset man, deep warm round baritone, slow Brooklyn drawl, audible wheezy inhale between lines, close dry mic, no reverb on the vocal. Beat: 90 BPM, heavily swung dusty boom-bap break, fat thudding kick, cracking dry snare, loose hats; a smoky after-hours electric piano and soul-jazz chord stab chopped into a short dark minor two-bar loop, pitched down; warm upright-bass-style low end; vinyl crackle and cassette hiss; a gritty scratched shout calls each number between the rules; sparse, ominous, late night, no chorus
exclude: singing, melodic hook, auto-tune, trap hi-hats, 808 slides, choir, bright pop synths, reverb-drenched vocals, high-pitched voice, fast double-time, female vocals
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, low and unhurried]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratched shout: one]
[Verse: laid back, horn-like phrasing, pause before the punchline]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratched shout: two]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratched shout: three]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: slow, spoken, beat drops out]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.
[End]
